headline: origins.test is still spoofable: DMARC does not enforce
fix: Publish a DMARC record for origins.test with a p=reject policy (or p=quarantine to start), e.g. at _dmarc.origins.test.
Make sure SPF and DKIM are in place first, so your legitimate mail still passes once DMARC enforces.
Then re-check to confirm the policy now enforces.

headline: www.origins.test is served directly at the origin 203.0.113.10: the CDN can be bypassed
evidence: at the origin 203.0.113.10 (Host: www.origins.test, certificate not checked): GET https://203.0.113.10/ -> 200
origin returned the same site as the CDN (matching body/title)
fix: Stop 203.0.113.10 from answering web requests sent directly to it: allow only Cloudflare's IP ranges at the firewall, or use an authenticated origin pull so the origin only serves requests that came through Cloudflare.
Or put www.origins.test's origin behind Cloudflare too, so there's no un-fronted way in.
Then re-check that www.origins.test can no longer be reached directly at 203.0.113.10.

headline: the origin 203.0.113.10 went silent (timed out) while the CDN still serves www.origins.test; likely a firewall dropping direct traffic, but a timeout can't prove it
evidence: at the origin 203.0.113.10 (Host: www.origins.test, certificate not checked): GET https://203.0.113.10/ -> Read timed out. (read timeout=10)
the CDN answered but the origin stayed silent for 10s; a firewall that drops (not rejects) non-CDN traffic does this, and so does a slow or overloaded server, so Akashi can't tell which

headline: origins.test is now protected: DMARC enforces (fixed since the scan)
